articles.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
articles.preview: OpenAI plans to continue investing heavily in AI data centers despite recent voter opposition. The company’s CFO stated that customer demand remains strong and that fundraising efforts will continue.

summary.t: Despite voters rejecting data center proposals in 10 states through 41 local ballot measures, OpenAI’s CFO, Sarah Friar, maintains the company’s investment strategy will proceed unchanged. Concerns about environmental impact, utility costs, and job losses fueled the opposition to data center development during the midterm elections.

OpenAI will continue to build relationships with hyperscalers and raise capital to meet customer demand for AI infrastructure. The company published a policy blueprint for its data centers, emphasizing a commitment to community engagement and trust-building.
OpenAI is currently seeking to raise up to $9 billion in additional funding at a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation.

articles.title: OpenAI bugging suspect Alfozan pleads not guilty
articles.preview: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI employee, has pleaded not guilty to charges of espionage. He is accused of planting a listening device at the company's San Francisco headquarters.

summary.t: Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, appeared in San Francisco federal court on Friday and pleaded not guilty to the charges. Following the brief hearing, he was remanded back into custody, a decision made since his arrest in early October. He has been held without bail throughout this period.

articles.title: Investors brace for lower Anthropic valuation, calling $1.5 trillion a 'stretch'
articles.preview: Investors are revising their expectations for Anthropic's valuation following recent market turmoil. The company's previously targeted $1.5 trillion valuation is now considered a significant stretch.

summary.t: The recent sell-off on Wall Street, particularly a more than 5% drop in the Nasdaq on Thursday, is fueling concerns about Anthropic’s potential valuation. This decline, the steepest in 19 months, reflects broader fears surrounding the AI sector and a potential slowdown in data center construction.

Stakeholders are now questioning Anthropic’s ambitious $1.5 trillion valuation, with one investor describing it as a ‘stretch.’ Previously, the company had aimed for a $2 trillion valuation in its upcoming IPO.

articles.title: Microsoft plans to use fewer neoclouds as AI buildout shows signs of strain
articles.preview: Microsoft is reducing its reliance on numerous cloud providers, focusing instead on expanding its own data centers. This shift comes amid concerns about the slowing growth of the artificial intelligence market.

summary.t: Microsoft is scaling back its partnerships with numerous neoclouds, including CoreWeave, Nebius, Chronoscale, IREN, Nscale, and Oracle. The company is prioritizing its own data center development. Microsoft is currently evaluating which neoclouds it will discontinue using. A key factor in this shift is Microsoft's desire to bolster its internal infrastructure.

The neocloud market has experienced significant volatility, with shares of CoreWeave, Nebius, and IREN declining by approximately 50% over the past month. Industry estimates suggest that around 323 neoclouds exist, and many are predicted to fail due to rising interest rates and concerns about excessive debt. Microsoft’s Azure cloud growth has also been impacted, with some contracts delayed until 2027.

In August, IREN transferred data center capacity to Microsoft, but a networking equipment upgrade pushed the infrastructure’s online date to January or February 2024. IREN reported AI revenue more than doubled to $200 million in the most recent quarter, representing a 16% share price increase on Friday.

articles.title: OpenAI, Arm and Qualcomm executives react to post-midterm AI sell-off
articles.preview: A sharp sell-off in tech stocks followed a post-midterm rally, fueled by fears of data center slowdowns. Executives from OpenAI, Arm, Qualcomm, and Box offered cautious responses to the market’s reaction.

summary.t: Following the midterm elections, stocks experienced a significant sell-off. The ‘Magnificent Seven’ lost over $1 trillion in market capitalization. Investors worried about potential data center constraints impacting business growth.

Arm’s CEO Haas dismissed the concerns as ‘very, very short term thinking,’ emphasizing the need for continued U.S. investment in data center expansion. OpenAI’s CEO Friar stated the company would continue investing in data center infrastructure and address community concerns regarding electricity costs. Qualcomm’s Amon noted that data center infrastructure is only one segment of the company’s business.
Several executives highlighted the ongoing demand for data center capacity.

articles.title: Marktbericht: Zweifel am KI-Geschäft belasten die Branche
articles.preview: Der weltweite Kursrutsch bei Tech- und Chipwerten schürt Zweifel, ob sich die hohen KI-Investitionen auszahlen. Gleichzeitig wächst vor dem geplanten Börsengang der Widerstand gegen die Billionenbewertung von Anthropic.

summary.t: Ein dramatischer Einbruch bei Chip- und Technologiewerten hat eine Verkaufswelle ausgelöst, die von den USA auch auf die Börsen in Asien und Frankfurt überschwappt. Der Handel in Südkorea musste zeitweise ausgesetzt werden. Die Sorge ist, dass sich der politische Kurs in den USA nach den Midterms ändern könnte. Finanzexpertin Lisa Hassenzahl sieht dies als "den Kater nach der Wahlparty". Nach der Erleichterung über politische Klarheit, ergibt sich nun die Sorge, dass Technologieunternehmen stärker reguliert werden könnten.

Der Widerstand gegen den Bau weiterer Rechenzentren für den KI-Boom ist bereits seit dem Wahlkampf spürbar. Kritisiert wird der enorme Stromverbrauch und die damit verbundenen Auswirkungen auf die Energiepreise sowie Lärm, Luftverschmutzung und Wasserknappheit. Zudem wird diskutiert, ob höhere Abgaben auf KI-Unternehmensgewinne angemessen wären.

Die Investoren zweifeln am Zeitplan für den Börsengang von Anthropic und fordern eine niedrigere Bewertung als die zuletzt diskutierten 1,5 Billionen US-Dollar. Die Initiierung einer Werbetour für den Börsengang könnte aufgrund der jüngsten Entwicklungen verzögert werden. Die Sorgen um die gesamte KI-Branche könnten durch eine Verschiebung der geplanten Emission verstärkt werden.

Der Kursverfall hat sich auch auf den DAX ausgewirkt, der am frühen Nachmittag bei rund 25.700 Punkten notiert. Der Index verzeichnete einen Minus von fast 2,4 Prozent. Viele deutsche Aktien, die zuvor vom KI-Boom profitiert hatten, wie Infineon, Siemens Energy und Hochtief, verzeichneten ebenfalls Verluste.

articles.title: Chinese AI lab Moonshot turned to Europe for Nvidia Blackwell access amid U.S. China curbs, sources tell CNBC
articles.preview: Chinese AI lab Moonshot is seeking access to Nvidia's Blackwell chips through European data centers. This move bypasses U.S. export controls aimed at limiting China's access to advanced AI technology.

summary.t: Moonshot AI, a Chinese AI lab, is exploring renting computing capacity from European neoclouds hosting Nvidia GPUs. Discussions have occurred this year for Moonshot to lease capacity from facilities in Europe. These facilities host Nvidia's Blackwell systems, currently restricted by U.S. export controls.

Due to U.S. restrictions on Nvidia's most advanced chips, Moonshot is utilizing overseas data centers to access Blackwell chips. This approach creates a loophole in export controls, allowing remote access without direct import. Current regulations lack broad authority to control access through overseas cloud services.

Moonshot is interested in leasing capacity for both inference and training, potentially utilizing clusters of 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs. Sources describe Moonshot as ‘very aggressive’ in its pursuit of increased computing power. Lease agreements typically involve upfront payments and ongoing fees.

articles.title: Insider: Zweifel an Werbetour: Börsengang von Anthropic wackelt
articles.preview: Der geplante Börsengang von Anthropic, dem Unternehmen hinter dem Chatbot Claude, steht aufgrund von Investorenzweitigkeiten in Gefahr. Die Werbetour zur Vorbereitung des Börsengangs wird nun möglicherweise verschoben.

summary.t: Die aktuellen Turbulenzen am Aktienmarkt, ausgelöst durch den Sieg der Demokraten bei den Midterms und den damit verbundenen Rückgang der Tech-Aktien, haben die Unsicherheit rund um den geplanten Börsengang von Anthropic verstärkt. Investoren zeigen nun deutlich mehr Skepsis gegenüber dem Zeitplan des KI-Startups.
Potenzielle Investoren fordern eine deutlich niedrigere Bewertung als die zuletzt diskutierten 1,5 Billionen Dollar.

articles.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
articles.preview: OpenAI is collaborating with cybersecurity firm Hacktron. The goal is to identify and address weaknesses in OpenAI’s systems.

articles.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
articles.preview: OpenAI has created a new benchmark, BioBasicsBench, to assess AI agent performance in scientific tasks. The benchmark consists of 100 tasks designed to evaluate AI’s ability to understand and work with real-world lab data.

articles.title: AI meltdown: Nvidia and Qualcomm drop more than 9%, pushing Nasdaq to worst day since April 2025
articles.preview: Nvidia and Qualcomm experienced significant drops, pushing the Nasdaq to its worst performance in nearly two years. Concerns about a slowdown in artificial intelligence development following the midterm election results fueled the market downturn.

summary.t: On Thursday, several chipmakers, including Nvidia and Qualcomm, experienced declines exceeding 9%. Nvidia’s market capitalization plummeted by almost $450 billion, and the Nasdaq Composite Index dropped 5.5%, marking its steepest decline since April 2025. This downturn was triggered by anxieties surrounding the potential slowdown in artificial intelligence development following the midterm election results.

The election results, particularly the Democratic sweep in key states with ambitious AI data center plans, contributed to increased market fears. Rising interest rates, substantial capital needs, and the Democratic victory in Congress are all seen as factors weighing on the market. Investment strategist Peter Boockvar noted that stock prices would be influenced by a slowdown in AI infrastructure development.

Meta President Dina Powell McCormick stated that building data centers would become more challenging following the election results. A victorious governor expressed a desire to meet quickly to secure investment and prevent job losses related to data center projects.

articles.title: Australian universities are creating AI-native graduates
articles.preview: Australian universities are shifting their approach to education, integrating AI directly into the curriculum. This initiative aims to produce graduates prepared for a future dominated by artificial intelligence.

articles.title: OpenAI pledges to halt NDAs in new data center policy proposal after election rebuke
articles.preview: OpenAI is revising its data center expansion strategy following a significant voter backlash. The company is abandoning non-disclosure agreements and prioritizing community input in its operations.

summary.t: In recent elections, voters across 10 states rejected proposals supporting the rapid expansion of AI data centers. Of 41 local ballot measures, 39 were voted down or restricted, signaling a strong public opposition to the development of these facilities.

OpenAI announced a new policy proposal that includes halting the use of non-disclosure agreements with public officials and soliciting community input for its data center projects. The company is also committing to publishing construction plans and encouraging policymakers to enact similar commitments.
OpenAI intends to cover the full cost of powering its data centers and is targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030.

articles.title: Musk spendete Rekordsumme: Amerikas Tech-Oligarchen regieren trotz Wahldebakel weiter mit
articles.preview: Fast 500 Millionen Dollar hat der reichste Mann der Welt in den republikanischen Wahlkampf gepumpt - und verloren. Doch auch nach dem klaren Sieg der Demokraten bleiben er und andere Tech-Oligarchen langfristig wohl die Gewinner. Die Gründe reichen über Trump hinaus.

articles.title: Nasdaq legt zu: KI-Werte erholen sich vom Kursgemetzel
articles.preview: Die Technologieaktien erholen sich am Markt, insbesondere im KI-Sektor. Ein starker Arbeitsmarktbericht hat die Spekulationen über weitere Zinserhöhungen verstärkt.

summary.t: Der Nasdaq-Index gewann am Freitag um 1,1 Prozent auf 24.579 Punkte. Der S&P 500 stieg um 0,3 Prozent auf 7377 Zähler. Der Dow Jones verlor hingegen 0,5 Prozent und schloss bei 51.286 Punkten.
Nach Kursverlusten am Vortag nutzten Investoren die Gelegenheit, in KI-Aktien zu investieren. Nvidia stieg um 3,6 Prozent, Advanced Micro Devices um 9,9 Prozent und Intel um 7,4 Prozent.

articles.title: Cramer’s week ahead: AI data center stocks face another hurdle and so does the Fed
articles.preview: Jim Cramer predicts continued challenges for AI data center stocks and anticipates another potential Federal Reserve interest rate hike. The market experienced a rebound Friday, but Cramer remains skeptical of a sustained recovery.

summary.t: Following a turbulent election week marked by investor shifts away from AI infrastructure companies, Jim Cramer believes the upcoming earnings reports from neoclouds will test investor confidence in the data center sector. He described Friday’s market rebound as a ‘dead cat bounce,’ indicating a lack of genuine recovery. Cramer highlighted ongoing concerns about data center spending and financing, suggesting these issues remain unresolved.

Several companies are reporting earnings next week, including Constellation Energy, On Holding, CoreWeave, Nebius, Corteva, Cisco Systems, and Applied Materials. Cramer’s focus is particularly on CoreWeave’s debt financing plans and Nebius’s new order activity. He emphasized the importance of seeing strong new orders and a robust project pipeline for companies like Nebius.

articles.title: AI stocks hammered by midterm shock as data center buildout becomes a 'war of attrition'
articles.preview: The US midterm elections have triggered a significant downturn in AI-related stocks, fueled by concerns about increased regulation and a potential slowdown in AI spending. Several key tech companies experienced substantial losses, highlighting the vulnerability of the sector to political shifts.

summary.t: Following the midterm elections, major tech stocks experienced a sharp sell-off. Nvidia lost 9.3%, AMD shed 17.3%, Microsoft dropped 3.6%, Micron fell 17.5%, Broadcom decreased by 10.4%, Tesla declined by 10.8%, and SpaceX experienced a 9.1% loss. These declines occurred on Thursday, coinciding with investor nervousness about the potential impact of a Democrat-controlled Congress on AI development.

Opposition to data center construction is growing, with dozens of local ballot measures in 10 states aiming to restrict their development. Between January 2024 and May 2026, at least 46 AI data center projects across 20 U.S. states, representing over $170 billion in investment, were blocked, withdrawn, or stalled due to community opposition. Analyst Kyle Rodda noted that these regulatory and political risks are exacerbated by existing market instability.

Market analysts report that earnings season has been disappointing, with the ‘Magnificent Seven’ companies undershooting growth expectations. Concerns about rising interest rates and overspending have led to negative cash flow for many hyperscalers. Goldman Sachs estimates AI-related capital spending could total approximately $7.6 trillion from 2026 through 2031, but the pace of investment is now viewed as potentially slowing.

summary.h: A ‘War of Attrition’ and Shifting Priorities
summary.t: Experts now view the AI buildout as a ‘war of attrition,’ with scarce power favoring companies with larger balance sheets.

articles.title: Weltweiter KI-Ausverkauf: DAX rutscht nach Rekordhoch ab
articles.preview: Der DAX erlebte einen drastischen Rückgang nach einer Rekordhoch. Ein weltweiter KI-Ausverkauf führte zu Verkäufen an den globalen Finanzmärkten.

summary.t: Der DAX verzeichnete nach einer Rekordhoch einen deutlichen Rückgang von rund 1,9 Prozent, was einem Minus von 1.000 Punkten entspricht. Dieser Abwärtsdruck wurde durch einen globalen KI-Ausverkauf ausgelöst, der sich auch in den US- und asiatischen Märkten widerspiegelte. Die Sorgen bezüglich der Rentabilität von KI-Investitionen trugen ebenfalls dazu bei. Der Handel in Seoul musste zeitweise unterbrochen werden, um Panikverkäufe zu verhindern.

Der Technologie-Sektor, insbesondere durch Aktien von Nvidia, AMD, Intel und Micron Technology, erlebte einen massiven Kursrutsch. Der Nasdaq 100 verzeichnete ebenfalls erhebliche Verluste. Die Unsicherheit bezüglich der KI-Euphorie und mögliche strengere Regulierungen beeinflussten die Aktienkurse stark.

Trotz überraschend starker Konjunkturdaten aus den USA, wie einem starken Arbeitsmarktbericht und einem hohen Verbrauchervertrauen, reagierten die Anleger kaum. Die Erwartungen einer Zinsanhebung durch die Federal Reserve schienen die Aktienmärkte nicht zu beeinflussen. Die politischen Unsicherheiten, insbesondere im Hinblick auf den US-Wahlkampf, trugen ebenfalls zur Marktvolatilität bei.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Tech-Boom ausgebremst - so können Anleger trotzdem profitieren
articles.preview: Der KI-Boom an der Börse hat sich verlangsamt. Hohe Zinsen stellen eine Herausforderung für Investoren dar.

articles.title: The AI ‘credit card’ is getting costlier as CoreWeave bond yield tops 16%
articles.preview: The cost of borrowing for AI data center builders is rising dramatically, with credit card terms becoming more restrictive. This shift reflects increased investor concerns about the future of AI spending and potential delays in data center projects.

summary.t: Credit markets are increasing interest rates on debt for AI data center builders. The yield on neocloud Coreweave’s 2032 bond has climbed above 16%, and credit default swaps for Nvidia, Broadcom, and Amazon have also risen significantly. Investors are demanding higher insurance premiums to protect against default, even for companies with strong credit ratings.

Political headwinds, including moratoriums proposed by Democratic governors in key states, are contributing to market anxieties. Goldman Sachs estimates that 45% of planned data center capacity could be impacted. Simultaneously, the market is seeing debt and equity movements aligning, raising questions about future credit availability.

Despite the rising costs, hyperscalers have issued a total of $67 billion in AI bonds since October, pushing total issuance to $296 billion this year. Goldman Sachs forecasts $440 billion of issuance next year, with an additional $300 billion in project-level debt.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Nasdaq deutlich im Plus - Tech-Aktien grün
articles.preview: Die US-Börsen erholen sich leicht von gestern, gestützt durch einen überraschend starken Arbeitsmarkt. Der Nasdaq-Index verzeichnete einen deutlichen Anstieg, während der Dow-Jones leicht fiel.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: Allgemeines Risk-Off an Börsen - umgekehrt Plus bei Chipwerten
articles.preview: Die europäischen Aktienmärkte erlitten heute einen deutlichen Rückgang. Besonders hervorzuheben ist der starke Anstieg der Werte im Halbleiterbereich.

articles.title: Der Börsen-Tag: "Blutbad" bei Tech-Aktien - was hat Politik damit zu tun?
Der Börsen-Tag: KI-Aktien erholen sich - hier eine Liste
articles.preview: Nach einem chaotischen Ausverkauf am Donnerstag erholen sich die KI-Aktien. Einige Titel legen heute vor dem Handelsbeginn zu.

articles.title: Nasdaq sell-off batters Asian chip stocks as SK Hynix, Samsung, Softbank, TSMC tumble
articles.preview: Asian technology stocks experienced a significant downturn on Friday, mirroring a sharp sell-off on Wall Street. Key chipmakers across Asia, including SK Hynix and Samsung, saw substantial losses.

summary.t: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% on Friday, triggering a correction, as investor concerns about artificial intelligence spending intensified. The index dropped below its recent peak by more than 10%.
Across Asia, several major chip companies suffered substantial declines. SK Hynix dropped 10.44%, Samsung Electronics fell 6.35%, and TSMC slid 4.69%.

articles.title: Chipaktien an den internationalen Börsen im freien Fall
articles.preview: Die globalen Aktienmärkte erleben einen starken Einbruch. Besonders betroffen sind Chip- und Technologieaktien, was zu Aussetzungen des Handels in Seoul und Frankfurt führte.

summary.t: Der Nasdaq 100 verzeichnete einen Tagesverlust von 6,4 Prozent, der stärkste seit dem Corona-Crash im März 2020. Auch der S&P 500 erlebte den schwächsten Tag seit April 2025. Experten sprechen von einem "Schwarzen Schwan" – einem unerwarteten Markteinbruch mit hoher Volatilität.

Der Einbruch wurde durch wachsende Zweifel an der Rentabilität von milliardenschweren Investitionen in Künstliche Intelligenz und den Bau von Rechenzentren ausgelöst. Die US-Demokraten-Sieg bei den Midterms verschärft die Debatte um Regulierung und Standortfragen.
Die Börse in Seoul wurde zeitweise ausgesetzt, um Panikverkäufe zu verhindern. Der DAX verlor im frühen Handel bis zu zwei Prozent und fiel unter die 26.000-Punkte-Marke.

articles.title: Panikverkäufe wegen KI und Öl : Börsen in Fernost sacken ab - TSMC, Samsung und SK Hynix leiden
articles.preview: Die asiatischen Börsen erleiden einen deutlichen Einbruch, getrieben von Sorgen um die Regulierung der Künstlichen Intelligenz. Zudem beeinflussen gestiegene Ölpreise die Marktentwicklung.

summary.t: Die Verkäufe an den US-Börsen haben sich auf die asiatischen Märkte ausgewirkt. Der südkoreanische Kospi brach um fast neun Prozent ein und fiel unter 5.000 Punkte. Auch in Taiwan und Japan gab es erhebliche Kursverluste.

Die Sorgen vor einer verstärkten Regulierung der Künstlichen Intelligenz, ausgelöst durch die US-Wahlen, haben die Anleger verunsichert. Neue Mehrheitsverhältnisse und politische Führungswechsel könnten Investitionen in Rechenzentren in Frage stellen.

articles.title: Jim Cramer explains why no AI stock seems safe from the market carnage
articles.preview: Jim Cramer believes uncertainty surrounding data center construction is driving a significant sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks. He argues that current valuations are unsustainable due to unclear future growth prospects.

summary.t: The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) experienced a dramatic drop, falling 3% on Wednesday and an additional 10% on Thursday. Alongside this, GE Vernova decreased by 7% and Sandisk plummeted 22% on Thursday.

Nvidia, a key AI chipmaker, is trading at approximately 12 times next year’s earnings with a projected growth rate of 70%. Cramer highlighted the risk that reduced data center construction could significantly impact these earnings projections.
Micron’s long-term take-or-pay contracts offer some revenue stability, but Cramer expressed doubt about their resilience if Micron or its customers faced financial difficulties.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says the AI sell-off isn't over, but it isn't another dot-com crash
articles.preview: Jim Cramer believes the recent AI stock sell-off is ongoing and will continue, but he dismisses comparisons to the dot-com crash. He advises investors to maintain a cautious approach while recognizing potential market improvements.

summary.t: On Thursday, Micron experienced a 17% drop, GE Vernova fell 7%, and Sandisk plummeted 22%. These companies also saw significant declines on Wednesday.

Growing opposition to new data centers following the midterm elections is fueling doubts about future AI infrastructure spending. This has contributed to the sharp decline in shares of companies involved in AI buildouts.
Smaller AI developers, including CoreWeave, Iren, and Nebius, face particular risks due to borrowing related to potentially delayed projects.
